title: Long-term follow-up of patients diagnosed with inflammatory rheumatic disease – Establishment of a cohort from North Rhine-Westphalia
summary:
Approximately 1.5 million people in Germany suffer from an inflammatory rheumatic disease. Inflammatory rheumatic diseases are a group of systemic disorders in which, in addition to joint and axial skeletal manifestations, internal organs may also be affected. Patients with an inflammatory rheumatic disease may experience a significant reduction in their quality of life as well as health-related absences from work.
The diagnosis of an inflammatory rheumatic disease and its complications is based on a clinical examination and the exclusion of other diseases through laboratory tests and/or imaging. Drug therapies to suppress the immune system are crucial for the long-term course of the disease. Your treating physician regularly documents your medical status, including disease activity and functional ability, as well as data on your social participation (e.g., receipt of sick pay, possession of a disability ID card). This data is collected partly by the physician and partly by you through questionnaires and is regularly stored in the electronic hospital information system. 
Neither in Germany nor internationally is there a database (registry) that provides information based on data collected in routine care from a superdiverse population, such as that characteristic of North Rhine-Westphalia. In particular, no long-term follow-up of patients with various inflammatory rheumatic diseases has been conducted to date.

This research project is being conducted to study the progression of chronic diseases. For patients with inflammatory rheumatic diseases, tracking disease activity and functional status, as well as comorbidities and social participation, plays a major role in the long-term course of the disease. The LORE Registry collects and scientifically analyzes, in a standardized manner, the medical data of adult patients with suspected or confirmed inflammatory rheumatic diseases. Data regarding your condition, treatment, and disease progression are collected. Clinical treatment data alone cannot fully capture the impact of the disease on your personal well-being and living conditions. For this reason, additional surveys are being conducted to assess your perception of your health-related quality of life and your living situation. The analysis of this data is intended to yield insights that will lead to a better understanding of the disease. These findings are intended to benefit the medical care of patients with inflammatory rheumatic diseases.
conditions: Diagnosis of an inflammatory rheumatic disease or a suspected diagnosis of an inflammatory rheumatic disease
